definitions.t_write_check_ns: Clock read of the final deadline check, taken immediately before the first Transport::write is called. Not a time inside the write call and not a send boundary.
definitions.t_boundary_ns: Clock read after write and flush returned. A send time only if SendTime::Qualified.
definitions.response_binding: Two layers. Connection: one request in flight per connection (AwaitingResponse until its response was completely framed and consumed; HTTP/1.1 in order; a connection with a misunderstood response is never reused). JSON-RPC body, HTTP 200 only: jsonrpc "2.0" and id equal to the request id (the BUY hash). HTTP 429 is bound by the connection alone; its complete HTTP body is consumed for framing but its contents are not interpreted. Any other non-200 status moves nothing.
definitions.ack: HTTP 200, matching version and id, and a result of exactly 0x followed by 64 hex digits (a bundle hash). Anything else is UnexpectedResult.

definitions.two_stage_send: After start_write and the BUY encoding the runner calls Transport::prepare with the complete request (TLS: encrypted into records in rustls, no socket I/O), then reads the clock for the final deadline check (t_write_check), then calls write, whose first action for a prepared TLS request is the first write_tls to the socket; flush drains the rest. A failure of prepare or a miss at the final check writes nothing to the wire and is Unknown with zero bytes, because the permit is consumed.
definitions.t_write_check_ns: Clock read of the final deadline check, after the transport prepared the request and immediately before the first Transport::write is called. Also returned by AdapterReport::t_socket_write_start_ns.
definitions.boundary: TlsTransport::flush returns once every ciphertext byte of the request was accepted by the kernel send(): the TlsUserspaceWriteFlushReturned boundary; says nothing about NIC or wire. TlsTransport::wire_bytes counts the bytes the kernel accepted on the connection.
definitions.request_size: TlsPolicy::max_plaintext_request_len is the largest HTTP request in plaintext bytes; Transport::max_request_len reports it and the dispatch refuses a larger frame before the admission (DispatchError::RequestTooLarge). The rustls output buffer is tls_output_capacity(max): plaintext plus 64 bytes per 16 KiB record plus 4 KiB.
definitions.eligibility: Ready only with a connection, no pending ciphertext and no prepared-but-unsent request, and idle time within max_idle; otherwise Stale.
definitions.maintenance: TlsConnectionOwner::connect and ::maintain resolve, connect, handshake, probe idle connections, give up overdue responses and reconnect; never called by a dispatch.
